name: Transient Congenital Hypothyroidism

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence reported in Asian and Middle Eastern populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Neonatal Screening and Confirmatory Testing Criteria

criteria.description: Elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels on neonatal screening
Low free thyroxine (T4) levels on confirmatory serum testing
Normal or transiently abnormal thyroid imaging (ultrasound or scintigraphy) indicating no permanent dysgenesis
Normalization of thyroid function tests within the first 3 years of life without ongoing treatment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated TSH and low free T4 on neonatal screening and confirmatory testing, plus evidence of transient thyroid dysfunction on imaging or follow-up
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of permanent congenital hypothyroidism by follow-up testing after 3 years of age.

pathognomonic.notes: Common early sign due to hypothyroidism-induced cholestasis

searchTerms: low muscle tone with delayed newborn reflexes
floppy muscles and slow reflexes in newborn
weak muscles and delayed neonatal reflexes

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties and poor sucking reflex
searchTerms: poor newborn feeding and sucking reflex

rare.symptomName: Hoarseness due to vocal cord edema
searchTerms: hoarse voice from swollen vocal cords
voice changes due to throat swelling
raspy voice caused by vocal cord edema

laboratory: Elevated serum TSH with low free T4 in neonatal period
Normalization of thyroid function tests within 3 years
Negative or transiently abnormal thyroid autoantibodies
imaging: Normal or transiently hypoplastic thyroid gland on ultrasound
Normal radionuclide uptake on thyroid scintigraphy
genetic: No consistent pathogenic mutations identified; transient hypothyroidism often non-genetic
other: Transient hypothyroidism resolves without permanent thyroid hormone replacement

distinguishingFeatures: Persistent hypothyroidism beyond 3 years of age
Permanent thyroid dysgenesis or dyshormonogenesis on imaging
Low or normal TSH with low free T4
May have other pituitary hormone deficiencies

redFlags: Persistent hypothyroidism beyond 3 years of age
Severe developmental delay or neurological impairment
references: American Academy of Pediatrics. Clinical Practice Guideline: Hypothyroidism in Infants and Children. Pediatrics. 2014.
Lazar L, et al. Transient congenital hypothyroidism: clinical and molecular aspects. Horm Res Paediatr. 2017.
